claim: Running multiple draft methods in parallel for speculative decoding is infeasible in practice because it requires substantially more GPUs, both to host the additional draft models and to verify their outputs.
falsifier: Estimate GPU memory and compute required for parallel draft methods versus a single draft method under fixed verification budgets.

conditions: multiple draft models must be hosted
outputs of each draft method must be verified
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Running multiple draft methods–GPU resource requirement boundary

claim: Using greedy sampling for both initial and self-critique generations improves the detection of RL-induced policy collapse by eliminating randomness and better revealing sharp policy distributions.
falsifier: Compare detection AUC of self-critique with greedy sampling versus stochastic sampling on a held-out contamination detection task; greedy sampling should yield higher AUC.

conditions: when using self-critique method that compares initial and critique responses
detection target is RL post-training contamination
exclusions: limited to the models, tasks, and RL training setups evaluated in the study

title: Greedy sampling for both for detection performance of RL

claim: Multi-agent collaboration improves outcome quality compared to single-agent execution in scientific idea generation tasks.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by comparing the performance of a multi-agent system against a single-agent system on the same scientific idea generation tasks, using the same LLMs and evaluation metrics.

conditions: in the context of scientific idea generation from a given topic
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (scientific idea generation), LLMs (GPT-4o, LLaMA3.1), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Multi-agent collaboration for outcome quality
